localFormats.name: DNI
localFormats.description: Documento Nacional de Identidad for Spanish citizens. Typical developer handling includes eight digits plus a control letter, preserving formatted and normalized representations.

localFormats.name: NIE
localFormats.description: Número de Identidad de Extranjero used for foreigner identification contexts. Common patterns use X, Y, or Z prefix, seven digits, and a control letter.

localFormats.name: NIF
localFormats.description: Número de Identificación Fiscal is the tax-identification concept. It may relate to DNI, NIE, or legal-entity identifiers, so do not treat it as one universal format.

localFormats.name: CIF legacy
localFormats.description: CIF is a historical term still present in legacy data and user language. Prefer current NIF terminology for legal-entity tax identifiers.

localFormats.name: NAF / Social Security number
localFormats.description: High-level developer context for Spanish social-security affiliation numbers. Business meaning and verification require official systems.

localFormats.name: Spanish postal code
localFormats.description: Five-digit postal code. The first two digits broadly align with province or autonomous-city prefixes, but postal validation is not administrative validation.

localFormats.name: Spanish phone numbers
localFormats.description: Phone data uses country code +34. Mobile, landline, and service ranges need dedicated parsing rules before validation.

localFormats.name: Spanish IBAN
localFormats.description: Spanish IBANs use the ES country prefix. The existing global IBAN Validator route is available for generic IBAN checks.

localFormats.name: BIC / SWIFT
localFormats.description: BIC/SWIFT codes identify financial institutions for international banking contexts. Do not infer domestic account ownership from a BIC.

localFormats.name: EU VAT / VIES
localFormats.description: Spanish VAT identifier syntax and EU VIES status checks are different concerns. VIES is a business-status lookup, not just string validation.

localFormats.name: Vehicle registration
localFormats.description: Informational overview for Spanish vehicle registration formats. Do not implement plate validation without a dedicated workbench spec.

localFormats.name: Bizum
localFormats.description: Domestic instant-payment experience commonly tied to Spanish banks and mobile numbers. Future tools should be informational unless a meaningful inspector is specified.

payments.title: EUR and Spanish IBAN
payments.text: Spain uses EUR and participates in IBAN-based European banking flows. Use the global IBAN Validator for generic checksum-level checks only.

payments.title: SEPA
payments.text: SEPA credit transfer and direct debit contexts matter for euro-denominated domestic and cross-border payment integrations.

payments.title: BIC / SWIFT
payments.text: International transfers may require BIC/SWIFT details in addition to account identifiers and payment purpose data.

payments.title: Bizum
payments.text: Bizum appears in Spanish consumer payment UX. Treat it as future product research, not a validation feature in this hub.

payments.title: Card payments
payments.text: Card flows use global payment-network behavior plus Spanish locale display conventions for amounts, receipts, and dates.

payments.title: Direct debit
payments.text: Direct debit usually intersects with SEPA mandates, creditor identifiers, account data, and authorization state.

payments.title: EU VAT / VIES
payments.text: VAT number format checks and EU VIES business-status lookups must remain separate in future workbenches.

validationRules.name: DNI
points: Eight digits plus control letter in common developer contexts
Formatted and normalized forms should be stored separately
Check-letter behavior is not identity verification

validationRules.name: NIE
points: Common prefix letters include X, Y, and Z
Uses digits and a control letter
Foreigner identification context differs from Spanish citizen DNI

validationRules.name: NIF
points: Tax identification concept, not one universal string shape
May represent personal or legal-entity contexts
Business verification requires authoritative systems

validationRules.name: CIF legacy
points: Legacy term appears in old data and user vocabulary
Current terminology should prefer NIF for legal entities
Migration logic should be explicit

validationRules.name: Postal code
points: Five digits
Province-prefix context is useful but not enough for address validation
Correos remains the official postal reference

validationRules.name: Phone
points: Country code +34
Mobile, landline, and service ranges differ
Normalize before comparison but preserve display format

validationRules.name: IBAN
points: Spanish IBANs start with ES
Checksum validation does not prove account ownership
SEPA and domestic payment context still matters

validationRules.name: VAT / VIES
points: Spanish VAT syntax and EU VIES status lookup are separate
VIES responses are business-status checks
Do not cache regulatory status without a product spec

commonMistakes.title: Treating NIF syntax as identity proof
commonMistakes.text: A valid checksum does not prove the person, company, or tax status exists.

commonMistakes.title: Losing CCC slices inside IBAN
commonMistakes.text: Spanish IBANs still contain bank, branch, check digits, and account slices useful for debugging.

commonMistakes.title: Using raw samples as labels
commonMistakes.text: Long CSV, JSON, IBAN, and invoice payloads belong inside inputs, not selector labels.

commonMistakes.title: Mixing decimal conventions
commonMistakes.text: Spanish business files often use comma decimals and dot grouping; API payloads may require normalized numeric values.

highlights.title: Spanish identity and tax IDs
highlights.text: DNI, NIE, NIF, legacy CIF, ES VAT, EORI, and social-security snippets are normalized with local evidence slices.

highlights.title: Payments and banking
highlights.text: Spanish IBAN, CCC, BIC, SEPA, Bizum, remittance, reconciliation, and statement snippets stay browser-only.

highlights.title: Developer QA surfaces
highlights.text: CSV, JSON, API payload, form, OCR, privacy, vehicle, and postal workflows expose field breakdowns for debugging.

developerNotes.title: Offline boundary
developerNotes.text: The suite validates structure and local evidence only; official status stays with AEAT, VIES, TGSS, DGT, Correos, banks, or payment providers.

developerNotes.title: Locale shape
developerNotes.text: Spanish UI data commonly combines DD/MM/YYYY dates, comma decimals, dot thousands, EUR, five-digit postal codes, and +34 phone numbers.

developerNotes.title: Debug-first output
developerNotes.text: Every workbench includes a dedicated field breakdown so implementers can see the exact detected Spanish slices.
